# World Models and Planning-Based Control

[Home](../../../../README.md) · [All categories](../../../README.md) · [简体中文](world-model-planning_cn.md)

Manipulation Action Models → Multi-Fingered Dexterous Hand Manipulation Research → Robot Manipulation Policies and Control → World Models and Planning-Based Control

Learn action-conditioned dynamics and use predicted outcomes to search or select robot actions toward a goal. Record interaction collection, action priors, planning and optional policy distillation; world modeling alone does not establish closed-loop control.

| [AM.MAN.DEX.POLICY.PLANNING.1] <a id="am-man-dex-policy-planning-1"></a> | **DSP｜In-hand manipulation · Autonomous interaction collection · World model + MPC**<br>[Dexterity from Supervised Play](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.22340v1)<br>Botao He, Yiming Dou, Yiannis Aloimonos, Jitendra Malik, Akash Sharma, Ruoshi Liu<br>**Tags:** `dexterous` [in-hand-manipulation](../../../topics/in-hand-manipulation.md) `autonomous-data-collection` `supervised-play` `behavior-cloning` `diffusion-policy` `world-model` `diffusion-forcing` `model-predictive-control` `policy-distillation` `real-world` | DSP behavior-clones a goal-free play policy from about 15 minutes of teleoperation, then collects hours of autonomous robot interaction to train a world model; at execution, the same play policy proposes action chunks, the world model predicts their outcomes, and MPC selects goal-reaching motions and replans for in-hand reorientation, with optional distillation into a fast direct-action policy.<br>**Evaluation scope:** Evaluated on planar Push-T and simulated/real cube reorientation. Hardware uses a Sharpa right hand with 22 joint-position commands; the main setup observes proprioception and tagged-cube pose, with an additional RGB-input experiment. Goals enter MPC scoring while the play policy and world model remain goal-agnostic. The hardware pipeline learns from real interaction rather than sim-to-real transfer. Distillation is an optional acceleration study; simulation distillation results and PPO comparisons are not all hardware validations. | arXiv v1 / 2026 | [Paper](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.22340v1) · [Project](https://play-policy.github.io/) | Initial reading<br>2026-10-24 |
| [AM.MAN.DEX.POLICY.PLANNING.2] <a id="am-man-dex-policy-planning-2"></a> | **DexHandDiff｜New-goal adaptation · Diffusion planning · Interaction-aware guidance**<br>[DexHandDiff: Interaction-aware Diffusion Planning for Adaptive Dexterous Manipulation](https://openaccess.thecvf.com/content/CVPR2025/papers/Liang_DexHandDiff_Interaction-aware_Diffusion_Planning_for_Adaptive_Dexterous_Manipulation_CVPR_2025_paper.pdf)<br>Zhixuan Liang, Yao Mu, Yixiao Wang, Tianxing Chen, Wenqi Shao, Wei Zhan, Masayoshi Tomizuka, Ping Luo, Mingyu Ding<br>**Tags:** `dexterous` `new-goal-adaptation` `diffusion-planning` `interaction-aware-guidance` `gradient-guidance` `contact-phase-guidance` `joint-state-action-diffusion` `dynamics-consistency` `dynamics-model` `llm-guidance-generation` [in-hand-manipulation](../../../topics/in-hand-manipulation.md) `receding-horizon-control` `simulation` | DexHandDiff designs interaction-aware guidance for dexterous diffusion planning: align the hand with an interaction point before contact, then guide state–action trajectories with goal and dynamics constraints, adapting to goals beyond the demonstrations by changing sampling guidance.<br>**Evaluation scope:** Task-specific joint state–action diffusion and separate dynamics models are learned from demonstrations. New goals primarily change denoising guidance without per-goal policy retraining. Door/tool tasks switch alignment and goal guidance using palm-to-interaction-point distance; in-hand tasks use single-phase goal, finger-motion and dynamics guidance. Consistency constraints reduce ghost object motion; generated actions execute with receding-horizon replanning. An LLM generates guidance code from environment descriptions; main scores use handcrafted guidance. Adroit/Shadow Hand simulation covers door, pen, hammer, relocation and block tasks, without reported hardware validation. Training only on 90° opening yields 59.2% across six opening/closing goals versus 29.5% for guided Diffuser. On four door angles, joint modeling plus dynamics guidance scores 31.7%, versus 67.5% for the complete interaction mechanism; these are not all-task means. Official resources provide partial implementation and an Adroit Door checkpoint. The first preprint appeared on 2024-11-27; this entry follows CVPR 2025/v6. | CVPR 2025 / arXiv v6 camera-ready / 2025 | [Paper](https://openaccess.thecvf.com/content/CVPR2025/papers/Liang_DexHandDiff_Interaction-aware_Diffusion_Planning_for_Adaptive_Dexterous_Manipulation_CVPR_2025_paper.pdf) · [Project](https://dexdiffuser.github.io/) · [Code](https://github.com/Liang-ZX/DexHandDiff) | Initial reading<br>2026-10-25 |
